text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned weakness and fatigue; to begin my assessment, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and do they persist throughout the day or come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 33-year-old woman. The patient reports feeling extremely fatigued and weak, especially towards the end of the day, to the point of difficulty in self-care. She mentions experiencing these symptoms currently. The patient has been traveling, hiking, and camping recently and notes having had multiple illnesses in the recent past.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. Given your recent travel, hiking, and camping, have you experienced any mosquito bites, fever, or muscle aches while out in the woods? Also, do you have a history of tick bites or Lyme disease?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Weakness and fatigue. I also have Mild diplopia.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. While the recent outdoor activity raises suspicion for tick-borne encephalitis or Lyme disease, the specific combination of profound weakness, fatigue, and new-onset mild diplopia (double vision) in a 33-year-old female is most characteristic of Myasthenia Gravis, an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction. I would like to confirm this with the Tensilon test or Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody levels.
